text:
sophia: quick follow-up from the intake v2 RFC — thinking about shrinking the handshake surface so runtime and bench can evolve independently. sketch below.

miguel: yep, wanted this. current adapter forces full bench run on every new model -> slows onboarding by hours.

tom_k: +1. what's the minimal contract you propose? also concerned about backcompat for dedicated customers.

sophia: minimal idea: two-phase admit
  1) metadata handshake (fast, <1s): model_id, arch, config_hash, tokenizer_hash, kv_fingerprint
  2) smoke probes (short seqs, latency/correctness) -> quick pass/fail
  full bench (longer) scheduled async with higher fidelity metrics

elaine: love the split. for quality gates we still need deterministic golden prompts for regression checks. can smoke probes catch subtle tokenization shifts? maybe add a tokenization sanitycheck in handshake.

miguel: +1 tokenization check. also suggest a lightweight ABI hash: export of input/output shapes + eos handling flags -> helps runtime detect incompatible model variants early.

raj: runtime note: if handshake only includes hashes, we need a clear fallback policy when a runtime sees unknown hash. propose: runtime tries compatible-variant routing -> if not found, fall back to host-model with throttled capacity and enqueue full bench.

yvonne: from customer side we need opt-in for async full-bench vs blocking admit. some orgs want stricter guarantees before any traffic.
sophia: agreed — make admit_mode a metadata flag: "blocking" | "async" | "canary"

bench-bot: quick-stats: simulated split-admit on staging: median onboarding time dropped 72%, false-positive smoke failures ~0.6% across 3k models.

tom_k: can we keep a single grpc endpoint but version the handshake proto? v1 -> old behaviour, v2 -> split admit. keep server side backwards compat.

sophia: yeah; proto sketch:
```
message HandshakeV2 {
  string model_id = 1;
  bytes config_hash = 2;
  bytes tokenizer_hash = 3;
  bytes kv_fingerprint = 4;
  enum AdmitMode { BLOCKING=0; ASYNC=1; CANARY=2 }
  AdmitMode admit_mode = 5;
}
```

elaine: one more: include sampling hint field (hot path vs long-context) so bench picks appropriate seq lengths by default.

miguel: tradeoff: more fields = better bench routing but more coupling. keep required fields minimal; make others optional hints.

raj: operational concern: store handshake records in a compact index for fast routing decisions. avoid large blobs (no full config dump).

yvonne: also surface admit state in console UI + webhook for infra teams.

sophia: next steps: I'll draft a small RFC PR with proto + short runbook (canary flow, fallback). will include migration plan for dedicated/private customers. comments? objections?

tom_k: no objections. add a versioned rollout plan and a toggle to force old behaviour per org.

elaine: add golden-prompt store retention policy (we hit storage costs). suggest 90d by default, configurable.

miguel: fine. i'll mock the bench-job scheduler changes and run a small experiment on staging.

sophia: awesome — thanks all. ping me if you want to pair on the proto or runbook. :thumbsup:
